title: 2014 AMC 12A Problem 18
statement: The domain of the function \[\tiny f(x)=\log_{\frac{1}{2}}\!\left(\log_4\!\left(\log_{\frac{1}{4}}\!\left(\log_{16}\!\left(\log_{\frac{1}{16}}x\right)\right)\right)\right)\] is an interval of length \(\dfrac{m}{n},\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is \(m+n?\)

solutions.text:
Working from the outside, \(f\) is defined exactly when \(\log_4\!\left(\log_{\frac{1}{4}}\!\left(\log_{16}\!\left(\log_{\frac{1}{16}}x\right)\right)\right)\) \(\gt0,\) which is equivalent to \(\log_{\frac{1}{4}}\!\left(\log_{16}\!\left(\log_{\frac{1}{16}}x\right)\right)\gt1.\)

Since the base \(\tfrac14\lt1,\) this means \(0\lt\log_{16}\!\left(\log_{\frac{1}{16}}x\right)\lt\tfrac14,\) hence \(1\lt\log_{\frac{1}{16}}x\lt16^{\frac{1}{4}}=2.\)

As \(\tfrac{1}{16}\lt1,\) this reverses to \(\left(\tfrac{1}{16}\right)^2\lt x\lt\left(\tfrac{1}{16}\right)^1,\) i.e. \(\tfrac{1}{256}\lt x\lt\tfrac{1}{16}.\) The length is \(\tfrac{1}{16}-\tfrac{1}{256}=\tfrac{15}{256},\) so \(m+n=15+256=271.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Peel the logarithms from the outside in, requiring each argument to be positive
Remember that bases below \(1\) reverse inequalities; translate each successive positivity condition before moving to the next inner logarithm
